items.title: The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children
items.desc: FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members, or recent members, of group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail It sounds benign: the Com, short for the Community. But crime agencies around the world warn that it is far from that and the young cybercriminals involved are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk. Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com. He was one individual operating from his bedroom in north-east England, but there are probably thousands more like him and parents are being urged by police to be aware and to check their children’s devices. Continue reading...

Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra has also reiterated his support for Rosebank, cautioning that “working-class people in vocational jobs” were threatened by the decline of the North Sea basin. items.title: Play about 12-year-old ecojustice influencer wins Shakespeare’s Globe prize
items.desc: Timothy X Atack wrote Tiny Alarms after workshops with children, who felt theirs would be the last generation of humans Tiny, a 12-year-old schoolgirl, is an ecojustice influencer, whose funny and disconcerting takes on the climate crisis go viral. She is also an alien, sent to warn humankind of its impending doom – but her mission is far more difficult than she anticipated. items.title: ‘Punched in the guts’: Poundland staff left reeling as it goes into administration
items.desc: Workers are sad but unsurprised as closures and job losses loom, while 2,000 suppliers will take a big hit Poundland staff fear they’ll be left out in the cold for Christmas. When will workers have a say in their future? “I feel Gordon Brothers punched us in the guts and took us down,” says Kelvin Blake, one of thousands of Poundland workers at risk of redundancy after the budget retailer’s US-based owners rejected at least two solvent bids for it. While administrators at AlixPartners, who were appointed on Wednesday, continue to consider bids for the whole group, which has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland including the Dealz chain, more than 10,000 staff and thousands of suppliers face a grim Christmas of uncertainty.
